text:
Aisha Khan: hi team - noticed my net pay is lower this cycle, looks like FICA was withheld twice on my RSU sell. can someone check?

Noah (People Ops): sorry to hear that Aisha. can you share the paystub lines (redact amounts if needed)? we'll pull payroll records.

Aisha Khan: redacted lines: 
```
Pay period: 12/01 - 12/15
Earnings:
 - Salary: $8,000.00
 - RSU Sell Proceeds (net of brokerage): $2,400.00
Taxes Withheld:
 - Federal Income Tax: $2,100.00
 - Social Security Tax: $496.80
 - Medicare Tax: $116.40
 - Social Security Tax (duplicate): $496.80
 - Medicare Tax (duplicate): $116.40
Net Pay: $6,189.60
```
I think the RSU net settlement was already net-of-FICA at broker level, but payroll also applied FICA.

Payroll Bot: Auto: payrun id pr-90122 completed. Parsed earnings show two tax events: one from regular payroll calc and one supplemental_tax event triggered by equity_integration adapter. Source: equity_adapter v2.3 mapped rsu_settlement -> supplemental_tax_code incorrectly marked "apply_fica=true".

Eve - Payroll: thanks for the details. quick triage: our equity integration should report RSU cash settlements as post-tax net proceeds (taxed at broker) and not subject to employer FICA withholding. Looks like the mapping change in equity_adapter v2.3 added apply_fica flag for settlement types. I'll pull the adapter diff and draft reversal.

Marc (Tax): from tax perspective, if employer withheld FICA erroneously, we have two remediation paths: 1) employer issues a refund to employee (off-cycle) for the excess FICA and then employer files Form 941-X for the quarter to claim refund of the employer portion and adjust deposits; 2) if timing allows, process correction on next payroll with reimbursable payroll correction and track for 941-X. Employer should also consider whether W-2 reflects correct totals; if the gross/taxable wage changes, a W-2c may be required at year-end.

Noah (People Ops): Aisha - will payroll do an immediate off-cycle reimbursement so you get the money back now?

Eve - Payroll: yes, plan: create an off-cycle payment to refund the duplicate FICA amounts (SS + Medicare employee share = $613.20). We'll also create reversing tax entries in the ledger. I'll tag Marc for the 941-X process. Aisha - you'll get a separate micro-deposit for $613.20 within 24-48 hours (subject to bank clearing).

Aisha Khan: thanks. please confirm whether this will change my year-end wage/tax totals and if I should expect a corrected W-2.

Marc (Tax): short answer: likely yes. If the RSU settlement is removed from taxable wages in our payroll ledger for that payrun, year-to-date wages and FICA withholding totals will change. We'll evaluate whether the adjustment triggers a W-2c; common approach is to prepare adjustment memos and file W-2c if year-end totals have already been finalized. If this is before year closure, it may be reflected on the original W-2. Payroll will open a W-2 review ticket with full audit trail.

Payroll Bot: queued off-cycle refund job pr-90122-refund for ts=1945679200.

Eve - Payroll: off-cycle draft stub: 
```
Reversal: FICA_dup_reversal -$613.20
Off-cycle pay: Refund_FICA $613.20
Notes: refund for duplicate employee FICA withholding on equity settlement. Audit ref: pr-90122 -> pr-90122-refund.
```

Eve - Payroll: processed off-cycle at 1945679400. refund payment initiated. ledger reversal entries posted. Marc - please advise on 941-X filing ownership.

Marc (Tax): I'll own the 941-X. I'll gather deposit timestamps and calculate employer share that we can reclaim. Expect initial draft of 941-X worksheet by EOD. I'll also coordinate with Legal if any state/local differences apply.

Payroll Bot: pr-90122-refund: SUCCESS. Payment status: pending bank settlement.

Aisha Khan: saw pending in my bank portal, thanks everyone. appreciate the quick fix.

Noah (People Ops): closing note: equity_adapter mapping reverted to previous config and flagged for a unit test to prevent reintroduction. Payroll/EQT teams to add integration test. Aisha - marking closed once 941-X ticket is queued and W-2 review created.

Marc (Tax): created ticket TAX-2026-33 for 941-X and W-2 impact; linking audit ref pr-90122.

Aisha Khan: thank you all :)
